validated_results.title: Effects of Black Raspberries and Their Constituents on Rat Prostate Carcinogenesis and Human Prostate Cancer Cell Growth In Vitro.
validated_results.reason: This study tested black raspberry constituents including urolithin A only in rat prostate carcinogenesis models and human prostate cancer cell lines in vitro, with no human participants.

validated_results.title: Co-carcinogenic effects of vitamin E in prostate.
validated_results.reason: The reported evidence on vitamin E comes exclusively from in vitro cell-line and rat/mouse experiments rather than original human observational or trial data.

validated_results.title: Main Inflammatory Cells and Potentials of Anti-Inflammatory Agents in Prostate Cancer.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of inflammatory cells and anti-inflammatory agents that mentions soy isoflavones without presenting original human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Association of the vitamin D metabolism gene GC and CYP27B1 polymorphisms with cancer susceptibility: a meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: Mushroom consumption and incident risk of prostate cancer in Japan: A pooled analysis of the Miyagi Cohort Study and the Ohsaki Cohort Study.
validated_results.reason: Pooled prospective Japanese cohort analysis reporting multivariable hazard ratios for prostate cancer incidence by frequency of mushroom consumption.

sample_size.excerpt: In the present study, a total of 36,499 men, aged 40-79 years, who participated in the Miyagi Cohort Study in 1990 and in the Ohsaki Cohort Study in 1994 were followed for a median of 13.2 years.

cases.excerpt: During 574,397 person-years of follow-up, 1,204 (3.3%) cases of prostate cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (1-2 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.92 [0.81, 1.05]; ≥3 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.83 [0.70, 0.98]; p-trend = 0.023).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (1-2 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.92 [0.81, 1.05]; ≥3 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.83 [0.70, 0.98]; p-trend = 0.023).

comparison.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer

design.excerpt: A pooled analysis of the Miyagi Cohort Study and the Ohsaki Cohort Study

timing.excerpt: Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was used to estimate multivariate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for prostate cancer incidence

continent.excerpt: among middle-aged and elderly Japanese men

ethnicity.excerpt: among middle-aged and elderly Japanese men

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Data on mushroom consumption (categorized as <1, 1-2 and ≥3 times/week) was collected using a validated food frequency questionnaire.

validated_results.title: The Microbiome and Prostate Cancer Risk.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of microbiome evidence in which dietary fiber metabolism is mentioned incidentally without original human incidence estimates.

validated_results.title: Commentary: Role of vitamin D in disease through the lens of Mendelian randomization-Evidence from Mendelian randomization challenges the benefits of vitamin D supplementation for disease prevention.
validated_results.reason: The report uses Mendelian randomization or genetic instruments, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: The Prevalence of Zinc Deficiency among Men with and without Prostate Cancer in Port Harcourt, Nigeria.
validated_results.reason: The study reports the prevalence of zinc deficiency and its association with disease severity among already diagnosed prostate cancer patients rather than prostate cancer incidence.
